mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D (4N14) engine replacement typically costs between £1,950 and £4,800 for the engine supply alone, depending on whether you choose used, reconditioned, or rebuilt. Supply and fit adds approximately £900-£1,300 in specialist labour. Dealer pricing can add 30-50% to these figures.

mainEntity.name: Is the 4N14 engine reliable? What are the common problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mitsubishi 4N14 is generally reliable but has three well-documented weak points. The most serious is balancer shaft coupling failure, which can cause timing chain sprocket breakage around 180,000 miles. EGR valve and DPF blockage are common on urban-driven vehicles, and timing chain tensioner wear can cause cold-start rattling.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical Outlander 2.2 DI-D is worth £3,000-£10,000. A rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,800 may represent a significant portion of the vehicle's value. If the car is in good condition, well-maintained, and you intend to keep it for 2+ years, replacement is often worthwhile. If vehicle value is under £4,000, evaluate scrap value first.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 4N14 and 4D22 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4N14 is the later, more advanced 2.2 DI-D engine (2010-2022) with MIVEC variable valve timing, available in 150hp and 177hp outputs. The 4D22 is the earlier 2.2 DI-D (2007-2010) with 156hp and no MIVEC system. The 4N14 has documented balancer shaft coupling issues that the 4D22 rarely suffers from, but both share common-rail diesel characteristics.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D has a timing chain, not a belt. This is a metal chain that should last the engine's lifetime, but there is a known design weakness: the balancer shaft coupling can fail, causing a timing chain sprocket to break. If you hear rattling on cold start or a loose-chain type noise under load, have the chain inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D engine replacement typically takes 2-4 working days. Specialist workshops can complete the job in 14-18 labour hours. Supply lead times vary: used engines 2-5 working days, reconditioned 5-10 working days, and rebuilt 7-14 working days. Confirm exact timelines with your chosen specialist.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D was introduced in 2007 as the flagship diesel offering in the Outlander range, featuring a 2.2-litre common-rail turbo diesel engine. It remained in production across the second-generation (CW) and third-generation (GG/GF/ZJ/ZK/ZL) chassis through to the Outlander's eventual discontinuation in 2022.

milestones.description: 4D22 (early 2.2 DI-D), 2.2-litre turbo diesel, 156hp - launched with second-generation Outlander
4N14 (revised 2.2 DI-D), 2.2-litre turbo diesel with MIVEC, 177hp - introduced with facelift
Third-generation Outlander launched; 4N14 continued with 150hp and 177hp output variants
Facelift; 4N14 updated to Euro 6b emissions standard, 150hp (110kW) / 360Nm torque
End of Outlander production; 4N14 remains available through specialist suppliers

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D (4N14) has well-documented weak points that can lead to costly repairs. The most serious is balancer shaft coupling failure, which is known to affect all 4N14 engines regardless of year. Timing chain, EGR, and turbo issues also drive replacement demand. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Balancer Shaft Coupling Failure - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D Timing Chain Breaks
problems.rootCause: A design weakness in the balancer shaft coupling system - the coupling fails, causing a timing chain sprocket to break. This can cause catastrophic engine damage if ignored. Mitsubishi's official repair kit costs over £3,000.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace balancer shaft coupling, timing chain, tensioner, and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Prevents catastrophic failure if caught early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt 4N14 with upgraded balancer shaft and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if valve/piston damage from chain break is confirmed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Outlander 2.2 DI-D of relevant age is worth approximately £3,000-£10,000 depending on mileage and condition. The replacement-to-value guidance is: - Vehicle worth under ~£4,000: scrap threshold - replacement may exceed vehicle value - Vehicle worth ~£4,000-£7,000: evaluate both; used engine may be better value - Vehicle worth ~£7,000+: replacement usually cost-effective
problems.recommendation: If you're still under 180,000 miles and don't yet have symptoms, the balancer shaft repair kit is a justifiable preventative investment - but note that it's costly. If the chain has already failed and caused valve/piston damage, replacement is the only safe route. Some specialists report the 4N14 can exceed 220,000 miles with careful maintenance, but the balancer shaft issue is an inevitable cost.
